text:
### Observed differences

- After A26, the immediate continuation shifted between two downstream activity pairs. In the earlier window, about 28 in 100 of A26's outgoing transitions led to A31 and about 24 in 100 to A33; in the later window, the share to A31 fell to about 18 in 100 while the share to A33 rose to about 32–33 in 100. In step with this, A30 and A31 each appeared in about 50 in 100 traces before and about 42 in 100 in the later window, while A32 and A33 each rose from about 50 to about 58–59 in 100 traces. [DIR016, OCC017, OCC018, OCC019, OCC020]
- Within these pairs the relative shares of the two directions also moved: from A30, transitions to A31 rose from about 45% to 58% while exits to A27 fell from about 55% to 42%; from A31, exits to A27 rose from about 45% to 58%; from A32, exits to A27 rose from about 47% to 56%; from A33, transitions to A32 rose from about 47% to 56% while exits to A27 fell from about 53% to 44%. [DIR019, DIR020, DIR021, DIR022]
- The A37–A38 cycle was traversed more often: A37 rose from about 1.6 to 1.8 occurrences per trace (repeated in about 37 in 100 traces before, about 42 in 100 in the later window) and A38 from about 0.8 to 1.0 occurrences per trace, now appearing in about 70 in 100 traces instead of about 57; A37 routed to A38 more often (about 48% vs 56% of its outgoing transitions, with A39 down from 52% to 44%), and A38 and A40 exited to A41 less often (about 62% vs 56% and 55%). [OCC023, OCC024, DIR024, DIR025, DIR026]
- The branch containing A01, A03, A04 and A05 lost share to the branch containing A02, A06, A07 and A08: the first group's activities each appeared in about 57 in 100 traces before and 49 in the later window, the second group's each rose from about 44 to 52 in 100, and the two groups' participations together sum to all 200 traces in each window. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008]
- Around A16–A19, A18 fell from about 53 to 46 in 100 traces and A17 from about 57 to 53, while A19 rose from about 47 to 54 and A16 from about 44 to 47; routing shifted accordingly, with A16 leading more often to A19 and less often to A18, A17 more often to A26 and less often to A18, A18 more often to A16 and less often to A26, and A19 less often to A16 and more often to A17. [OCC013, OCC014, OCC015, OCC016, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012, DIR013]
- A34 was executed in fewer traces (about 19 in 100 before, about 12–13 in the later window), consistent with A35 routing to A36 more often (about 62% vs 71% of its outgoing transitions) and to A34 less often (about 38% vs 29%). [OCC021, DIR023]
- Smaller movements with weak support: slight decreases for A10–A13, and the near-even splits around A21/A22 and A28/A29 moved by about 2–3 percentage points. [OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, OCC012, DIR014, DIR017, DIR018]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, the alternative routes after A26 are taken with different frequencies: the route into the A31/A30 pair is entered less often (its share of A26's outgoing transitions fell from about 28 in 100 to about 18 in 100, with A30 and A31 appearing in about 42 in 100 traces instead of 50), while the route into the A33/A32 pair is entered more often (about 24 rising to about 32–33 in 100 of A26's outgoing transitions, with A32 and A33 rising from about 50 to about 58–59 in 100 traces). All four downstream activities remain frequent in both windows, so only the shares between existing alternatives change; the participation and direction indicators agree in direction, and the key differences are larger than in about 93–95 out of 100 random re-splits of the same data. [DIR016, OCC017, OCC018, OCC019, OCC020, DIR019, DIR020, DIR021, DIR022]

Limitations: the occurrence and direction items summarise the same traces, so they corroborate rather than independently confirm one another, and no expected-by-chance baseline is provided in the evidence; with 200 traces per window, sampling variation or a variant concentrated in one window cannot be excluded entirely, although the mirrored, coordinated pattern of these items makes pure chance an unlikely explanation for the cluster as a whole. [DIR016, OCC017, OCC019, DIR019]

Other differences:
- The A37–A38 cycle is traversed more often in the later window, with less continuation from A37 to A39 and less exit to A41 from A38 and A40. [OCC023, OCC024, DIR024, DIR025, DIR026]
- The branch A01/A03/A04/A05 (about 57 in 100 traces before, 49 in the later window) lost share to the branch A02/A06/A07/A08 (about 44 rising to 52 in 100). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008]
- Around A16–A19, A18 and A17 are executed in fewer traces while A19 and A16 gain, with matching shifts in the outgoing transitions of A16, A17, A18 and A19. [OCC013, OCC014, OCC015, OCC016, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012, DIR013]
- A34 is executed in fewer traces as A35 more often leads to A36. [OCC021, DIR023]
- Smaller, weakly supported movements concern A10–A13 and the near-even splits around A21/A22 and A28/A29. [OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, OCC012, DIR014, DIR017, DIR018]
